knowledge_statements.title: Practical Predictor-Corrector Theory Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between safeguarded polynomial path following and unsafeguarded practical predictor-corrector choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A predictor-corrector QP method inherits a polynomial path-following bound only if its accepted step preserves the neighborhood, positivity, and complementarity-decrease conditions used by that bound. A practical rule that chooses the centering parameter from an affine-scaling prediction and then accepts a fraction-to-boundary step does not, by that rule alone, imply \[\mu_{k+1}\le\left(1-\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt m}\right)\mu_k\] or invariance of any prescribed central-path neighborhood. Therefore the standard polynomial iteration theorem cannot be asserted for the unsafeguarded heuristic. It becomes applicable only after adding safeguards and proving the required invariants for the resulting algorithm.

children.title: Infeasible-Start Initialization
children.top_down_role: Initialization allowing primal or dual residuals before path tracking.

assumptions_latex: Step length is chosen solely to preserve strict positivity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of fraction-to-boundary safeguarding in an infeasible-start method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fraction-to-boundary step guarantees only \(s^{k+1}>0\) and \(z^{k+1}>0\). Without a merit, filter, central-neighborhood, or other globalization rule and suitable regularity, it does not imply decrease of the primal residual, dual residual, or complementarity and supplies neither convergence nor an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping slacks and multipliers positive does not by itself reduce residuals, prove convergence, or certify infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Positivity Is Not Globalization

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^0,y^0,s^0,z^0)\text{ lies in the complementarity interior although }r_p^0\text{ and }r_d^0\text{ may be nonzero}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of an algebraic infeasible start with positive complementarity variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary finite \(x^0,y^0\), any \(s^0>0\) and \(z^0>0\) define a complementarity-interior algebraic iterate when the mismatches are retained as residuals \(r_p^0=(Ax^0-b,\,Gx^0+s^0-h)\) and \(r_d^0=Qx^0+c+A^{\mathsf T}y^0+G^{\mathsf T}z^0\). Thus an infeasible start requires positivity of complementarity variables, not satisfaction of the original affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite primal and equality-dual guesses can be paired with positive slacks and multipliers while violations are carried explicitly as residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Absorbing Positive Initialization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mehrotra-type direction variant from a positive residual-infeasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \((x,y,s,z)\) with \(s,z>0\), first solve the primal-dual Newton equations with complementarity right-hand side \(-Sz\) to obtain an affine direction. Compute maximal positivity-preserving affine steps and predicted complementarity \(\mu_a\), and choose a declared \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), commonly \(\sigma=(\mu_a/\mu)^3\). Resolve the same Newton matrix with complementarity right-hand side \(-Sz+\sigma\mu\mathbf1-\Delta S^a\Delta z^a\), retaining the primal and dual residual right-hand sides. Take declared fraction-to-boundary primal and dual steps. A separate acceptance or neighborhood rule is required for convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine predictor estimates complementarity reduction, and a second solve adds centering and the second-order complementarity correction.
assumptions_latex: Both Newton systems are solved to their prescribed tolerances.
A separate globalization or neighborhood policy governs acceptance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s^+>0,\ z^+>0\text{ for fraction-to-boundary steps, without an unconditional convergence claim.}
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Start Predictor-Corrector Direction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual behavior of a common damped step from an infeasible primal-dual iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the Newton direction satisfy \[A\Delta x=-r_A,\qquad G\Delta x+\Delta s=-r_G,\qquad Q\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+G^{\mathsf T}\Delta z=-r_d.\] For the common update \((x,y,s,z)^+=(x,y,s,z)+\alpha(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s,\Delta z)\), the affine residuals obey \[r_A^+=(1-\alpha)r_A,\qquad r_G^+=(1-\alpha)r_G,\qquad r_d^+=(1-\alpha)r_d.\] This identity does not establish complementarity reduction, step acceptance, or global convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common damped Newton step contracts the linear primal and dual residuals exactly when their equations use the full negative residuals.
assumptions_latex: The QP data are fixed during the update.
One common step length \(\alpha\) is used for all displayed variables.

notation.meaning: Equality, slack-form inequality, and stationarity residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Affine-Residual Contraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of distinct primal and dual step lengths in an infeasible-start Newton update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Q\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+G^{\mathsf T}\Delta z=-r_d\). Update \((x,s)\) with step \(\alpha_p\) and \((y,z)\) with step \(\alpha_d\). Then \[r_d^+=(1-\alpha_d)r_d+(\alpha_p-\alpha_d)Q\Delta x.\] If also \(A\Delta x=-r_A\) and \(G\Delta x+\Delta s=-r_G\), then \(r_A^+=(1-\alpha_p)r_A\) and \(r_G^+=(1-\alpha_p)r_G\). Thus exact common-step stationarity contraction generally fails when \(\alpha_p\ne\alpha_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate primal and dual steps preserve primal-residual contraction, but stationarity gains a curvature correction unless the steps coincide.
assumptions_latex: The QP data remain fixed during the update.
The displayed full-residual Newton equations are satisfied.

Infeasible-Start Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-slack initialization permitting nonzero primal and dual residuals before convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose arbitrary \(x^0,y^0\) and strictly positive \(s^0,z^0\), and define \[r_p^0=(Ax^0-b,\,Gx^0+s^0-h),\qquad r_d^0=Qx^0+c+A^{\mathsf T}y^0+G^{\mathsf T}z^0.\] At iteration \(k\), solve a primal-dual Newton system whose right-hand side reduces \(r_p^k\), \(r_d^k\), and \(S_kz^k-\sigma_k\mu_k\mathbf1\). Choose a fraction-to-boundary step maintaining \(s^{k+1},z^{k+1}>0\). Stop only when the primal residual, dual residual, and complementarity satisfy their stated tolerances; positivity of the initial slacks alone is not a feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize positive slacks and multipliers even with nonzero feasibility residuals, then use damped Newton steps to reduce feasibility and complementarity simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: The initial slacks and inequality multipliers satisfy \(s^0,z^0>0\).
Each Newton system admits a direction satisfying the selected residual-reduction equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method permits \(r_p^0\ne0\) or \(r_d^0\ne0\) while preserving positive complementarity variables during the iteration.

notation.meaning: Combined primal equality and slack residual.

assumptions_latex: Strict feasibility is tested against the displayed inequality representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{ri}(P)\ne\varnothing\ \not\Rightarrow\ \exists x:Ax=b,\ Gx<h\text{ in an unreduced representation}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of identically active or opposing redundant inequalities on a literal strict-feasibility Phase I.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a displayed inequality is an identity on the equality affine space, or opposing redundant inequalities force an equality, no point satisfies every displayed inequality strictly even when the feasible set has nonempty relative interior. Such rows must be recognized as affine-hull equalities or removed before the common-margin Phase I is interpreted as a relative-interior test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant or identically active inequalities can make literal strict feasibility impossible despite a nonempty relative interior.
knowledge_statements.title: Literal-Strictness Formulation Boundary

assumptions_latex: The equality affine space \(\{x:Ax=b\}\) is nonempty.
The auxiliary optimal value is finite, and an approximate sign declaration uses certified bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t^*>0\iff\exists x:Ax=b,\ Gx<h;\qquad t^*=0\iff\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\ne\varnothing\text{ and no strict point exists};\qquad t^*<0\iff\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact status interpretation of the primal common-margin auxiliary problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\{x:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\) and a finite optimum \[t^*=\max\{t:Ax=b,\ Gx+t\mathbf1\le h\}.\] Then \(t^*>0\) exactly when a point satisfies \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx<h\). If \(t^*=0\), the original inequalities are feasible but admit no strictly feasible point. If \(t^*<0\), the original affine inequality system is infeasible. When computed approximately, these conclusions require certified lower or upper bounds that determine the relevant sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum common margin is positive exactly for strict feasibility, zero for feasible boundary-only systems, and negative for infeasibility, under the stated assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Common-Margin Classification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Required branch before interpreting an inequality-margin Phase-I problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Before solving a margin problem constrained by \(Ax=b\), either exhibit \(x_e\) with \(Ax_e=b\), or exhibit \(y\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\). The first outcome establishes a nonempty equality affine space; the second certifies that \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent, so no inequality-margin value should be used for status classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase I must first establish equality consistency; a left-null-space witness certifies inconsistent equalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Consistency Precheck

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerically certified interpretation of a common-margin Phase-I solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let certified bounds \(L\le t^*\le U\) be available for the finite common-margin optimum. Then \(L>0\) certifies strict feasibility, \(U<0\) certifies infeasibility of the displayed inequalities relative to \(Ax=b\), and \(L=U=0\) certifies boundary-only feasibility. If \(0\in[L,U]\) with \(L<U\), the computation does not distinguish these statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified interval determines the margin sign only when it lies strictly on one side of zero or collapses exactly to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) and \(U\) are verified lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L>0\Rightarrow t^*>0;\quad U<0\Rightarrow t^*<0;\quad 0\in[L,U],\ L<U\Rightarrow\text{status unresolved}.

notation.meaning: Certified enclosure of the optimal common margin.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of the Common-Margin Phase-I Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual formulation and bounds for the finite common-margin auxiliary problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[t^*=\max_{x,t}\{t:Ax=b,\ Gx+t\mathbf1\le h\},\] a dual is \[\min_{y,z}\ b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z\quad\text{subject to}\quad A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\quad \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z=1,\quad z\ge0.\] Every dual-feasible \((y,z)\) supplies \(t^*\le b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z\). Under the standard finite feasible linear-programming regime, optimal primal and dual values coincide and are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized nonnegative inequality multipliers form the dual margin problem and provide certified upper bounds on the achievable strict-feasibility margin.
assumptions_latex: The primal common-margin problem is feasible and has a finite optimum.
Strong-duality conclusions are invoked only in the standard finite feasible linear-programming regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t^*\le b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z\quad\text{for every dual-feasible }(y,z).
knowledge_statements.title: Dual of the Common-Margin Phase-I Problem

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Automatic Primal-Interior Start for the Margin Auxiliary Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict initialization of the common-margin auxiliary inequalities after equality consistency is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_e\) with \(Ax_e=b\), choose any \[t_0<\min_i\{h_i-(Gx_e)_i\}.\] Then \((x_e,t_0)\) satisfies \(Ax_e=b\) and \(Gx_e+t_0\mathbf1<h\), so it is a strictly inequality-feasible starting point for a primal barrier treatment of the common-margin auxiliary problem. This construction does not itself produce dual feasibility or specify a complete primal-dual path-following method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once an equality-feasible point is known, choosing a sufficiently negative margin variable strictly satisfies every auxiliary inequality.
assumptions_latex: The displayed inequality set is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Primal-Interior Start for the Margin Auxiliary Problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession condition under which the common-margin auxiliary problem has no finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(Ax_e=b\) for some \(x_e\). The common-margin problem \[\sup\{t:Ax=b,\ Gx+t\mathbf1\le h\}\] is unbounded above if and only if there exist \(d\) and \(\tau>0\) such that \(Ad=0\) and \(Gd+\tau\mathbf1\le0\). By positive scaling, this is equivalent to the existence of \(d\) with \(Ad=0\) and \(Gd+\mathbf1\le0\). In this regime finite-sign classification of \(t^*\) is inapplicable, although sufficiently large points on the recession path are strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The margin optimum is infinite exactly when an equality-feasible recession direction improves every displayed inequality margin uniformly.
assumptions_latex: The equality affine space is nonempty.
The displayed inequality family is finite and nonempty.

notation.meaning: Positive uniform margin growth along a recession direction.

Phase-I Interior Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary max-margin phase for finding a strictly feasible point for the QP inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the equality system \(Ax=b\) is feasible. Solve the auxiliary convex problem \[\max_{x,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\qquad Gx+t\mathbf1\le h\] by an interior method, stopping with a certified bound on its optimal value \(t^*\). If a computed feasible pair has \(t>0\), then \(x\) is strictly feasible for \(Gx<h\) and may initialize a primal interior method. If the certified upper bound satisfies \(t^*\le0\), this phase cannot produce strict primal feasibility. A primal-dual feasible-start method additionally requires an analogous dual phase or a joint auxiliary formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize a common inequality margin under the equalities; a positive certified margin supplies a strictly feasible primal point, while a nonpositive optimum rules out such a margin.
assumptions_latex: The auxiliary optimum is finite and its reported bound is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t>0\) implies \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx<h\); a certified \(t^*\le0\) implies no point has a positive common margin.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual-feasible normalized multiplier with \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z\le0\) gives \(t^*\le0\), and a strictly negative bound gives \(t^*<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed certificate is already an immediate instance of the accepted common-margin dual bound.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of Dual of the Common-Margin Phase-I Problem hold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-data checks required before interpreting an embedding output as primal infeasibility or primal unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), with \(Q\succeq0\): \(A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0\) certify primal infeasibility. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy condition for recovering an original-QP solution from a positive embedding scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an embedding uses homogeneous variables \((u,\tau)\) and a residual block satisfies \(R_{\mathrm{emb}}(u,\tau)=\tau R_{\mathrm{QP}}(u/\tau)\) for \(\tau>0\). Then \[\|R_{\mathrm{QP}}(u/\tau)\|=\frac{\|R_{\mathrm{emb}}(u,\tau)\|}{\tau}.\] Hence an absolute embedded tolerance independent of \(\tau\) does not certify an accurate dehomogenized solution when \(\tau\) is small; the sufficient test is \(\|R_{\mathrm{emb}}\|\le\tau\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embedding residuals are amplified by division by the solution scale, so reliable dehomogenization requires residual accuracy proportional to that scale.
knowledge_statements.title: Dehomogenized Residual Reliability Condition
Embedding-Based QP Status Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status interpretation for homogeneous embeddings that couple optimization variables with scale variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An embedding-based convex-QP method augments the primal-dual equations with nonnegative scalars \(\tau\) and \(\kappa\), maintains a homogeneous feasibility system, and drives its embedded complementarity to zero. At a limiting nonzero embedded solution, \(\tau>0\) permits dehomogenization by division by \(\tau\), yielding a primal-dual QP solution. If \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\), the remaining normalized variables must instead satisfy explicitly checked Farkas or recession-ray conditions before infeasibility or unboundedness is declared. If both scale variables approach zero without a normalized certificate, the embedding does not by itself determine status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive solution scale yields an optimal QP solution; a positive certificate scale at zero solution scale may yield infeasibility or unboundedness only after certificate checks.
assumptions_latex: The chosen homogeneous embedding is algebraically equivalent to the QP KKT system when \(\tau>0\).
Reported status certificates are normalized and checked against the original QP data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau>0\) supports optimal-solution recovery, whereas \(\tau=0\), \(\kappa>0\) supports a nonoptimal status only through a valid original-data certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex QP residual certificate with explicit inequality slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c,x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b,y\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(h,s,z\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider the convex quadratic program \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx+s=h\), with \(s\ge0\). For a candidate \((x,s,y,z)\) with \(s,z\ge0\), define \(r_p=(Ax-b,Gx+s-h)\), \(r_d=Qx+c+A^Ty+G^Tz\), and \(r_c=Sz\), where \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\). The inequalities \(\|r_p\|\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\|r_d\|\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(\|r_c\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_c\) form a directly checkable approximate KKT certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small primal, stationarity, and complementarity residuals, together with nonnegative slacks and multipliers, certify approximate satisfaction of the convex QP KKT system.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(G\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r_p\|\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\|r_d\|\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(\|Sz\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_c\) certify approximate primal feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity.

The norms and scale formulas are part of the certificate: enlarging freely chosen denominators can make \(\rho\) arbitrarily small without improving the candidate point.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\), suppose \(Ax=b\), \(Gx+s=h\), \(s,z\ge0\), and \(Qx+c+A^Ty+G^Tz=0\). Hence \(s^Tz\le\varepsilon_g\) is a verifiable certificate that the feasible primal objective lies within \(\varepsilon_g\) of the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible stationary primal-dual pair, the duality gap equals total complementarity; a small gap therefore certifies near-optimality.

children.title: Primal Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Ray, alternative-system, and embedding evidence for an empty primal feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-aware sufficient validation of an approximate primal-infeasibility ray when a global feasible-point norm bound is known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\ge0\), \(\eta=-(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z)>0\), and \(r=A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\). If every putative feasible point is known a priori to satisfy \(\|x\|\le R\) and \(\eta>R\|r\|_*\), then no \(x\) satisfies \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\). Without a verified error bound of this kind, a small cancellation residual and negative right-hand-side pairing do not constitute a rigorous certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate Farkas ray is rigorous only when its separation margin dominates a verified worst-case cancellation error.
assumptions_latex: The bound \(\|x\|\le R\) holds for every putative feasible point.
\(\|\cdot\|_*\) is dual to the norm used for \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z)>R\|A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\|_*\Rightarrow\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Approximate Farkas Validation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small Cancellation Residual Alone Is Not a Farkas Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of tolerance-only validation on an unbounded affine domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\delta>0\), the system \(\delta x\le-1\) is feasible, but with \(z=1\) its cancellation residual is \(\|G^{\mathsf T}z\|=\delta\) and its right-hand-side pairing is \(h^{\mathsf T}z=-1<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily small cancellation residual plus a negative pairing does not prove infeasibility without a verified bound controlling the residual error.

notation.meaning: Arbitrarily small constraint coefficient and cancellation residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Small Cancellation Residual Alone Is Not a Farkas Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalization of an Exact Farkas Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale normalization for a strict mixed-affine infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(z\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\), and \(\beta=b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0\), then \[(\widehat y,\widehat z)=\frac{1}{-\beta}(y,z)\] satisfies \(\widehat z\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+G^{\mathsf T}\widehat z=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+h^{\mathsf T}\widehat z=-1\). Conversely, every certificate normalized to pairing \(-1\) is an exact unnormalized certificate. This removes arbitrary positive scaling and supplies a fixed separation target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exact Farkas ray with negative right-hand-side pairing can be scaled so that the pairing equals minus one.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier pairing is strictly negative.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization of an Exact Farkas Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact theorem of alternatives for the fixed equality-and-less-than inequality convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite-dimensional real data \(A,b,G,h\), exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \[(i)\quad Ax=b,\qquad Gx\le h;\] \[(ii)\quad A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad z\ge0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0.\] Equivalently, the strict pairing in (ii) may be normalized to \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed affine system is infeasible exactly when it has a normalized Farkas multiplier ray with zero aggregate normal and negative right-hand-side pairing.
assumptions_latex: Equality multipliers are unrestricted and inequality multipliers are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}=\varnothing\iff\exists(y,z):z\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z=-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Affine Farkas Alternative

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^Ty+G^Tz=0\) and \(b^Ty+h^Tz<0\) certify that the primal constraints are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for infeasibility of affine equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the affine constraint system \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), a primal-infeasibility certificate is a pair \((y,z)\) satisfying \(z\ge0\), \(A^Ty+G^Tz=0\), and \(b^Ty+h^Tz<0\). These conditions are finitely checkable. Indeed, they separate the affine image of every putative feasible point from the prescribed right-hand sides, so their satisfaction certifies that no \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) obeys all primal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas multiplier pair with zero aggregated constraint normal and a strictly negative right-hand-side pairing certifies that the primal affine constraints are inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Infeasibility Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed Farkas certificate is consistent with the stated Gx<=h convention, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied. An authoritative alternative-theorem or QP-certificate reference is required.

children.title: Dual Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Status evidence associated with dual inconsistency or primal recession behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status boundary for the displayed convex-QP dual system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dual infeasibility means that no tuple satisfies the displayed dual feasibility and stationarity conditions. It must not be reported when dual-feasible points or sequences exist but the dual supremum is unattained. A homogeneous recession witness may exclude every dual-feasible tuple, but interpreting it as primal unboundedness additionally requires a primal feasible base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual infeasibility is absence of every dual-feasible point, not failure to attain a feasible dual supremum; primal unboundedness additionally needs primal feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual systems use one fixed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility versus Dual Nonattainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonstrict Recession Pairing Is Not a Dual-Infeasibility Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary on the strict cost inequality in a recession witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conditions \(Qd=0\), \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d=0\) do not certify dual infeasibility. The unconstrained QP \(\min_x0\) has \(Q=0\), \(c=0\), admits every nonzero \(d\), and has a feasible stationarity system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero cost pairing is compatible with dual feasibility; strict negativity is essential.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonstrict Recession Pairing Is Not a Dual-Infeasibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalization of a Dual-Infeasibility Recession Witness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale normalization for an exact homogeneous recession certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(d\ne0\) satisfies \(Qd=0\), \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), then \(\widehat d=d/(-c^{\mathsf T}d)\) satisfies the same homogeneous equalities and inequalities and \(c^{\mathsf T}\widehat d=-1\). Conversely, every witness normalized by \(c^{\mathsf T}d=-1\) is an unnormalized witness. The normalization removes arbitrary positive scaling and supplies a fixed validation target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exact negative-cost recession witness can be scaled so that its cost pairing equals minus one.
assumptions_latex: The certificate uses the fixed convention \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\).
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization of a Dual-Infeasibility Recession Witness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual-Stationarity Alternative for a Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact alternative between feasibility of the convex-QP dual stationarity system and a negative-cost recession witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\). Exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \[(i)\quad Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad z\ge0;\] \[(ii)\quad Qd=0,\qquad Ad=0,\qquad Gd\le0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}d<0.\] Equivalently, system (ii) may be normalized by \(c^{\mathsf T}d=-1\). Thus absence of every dual-feasible stationary tuple is equivalent to existence of a normalized negative-cost recession witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-semidefinite QP, the dual stationarity system is infeasible exactly when a normalized zero-curvature negative-cost recession witness exists.
assumptions_latex: The fixed convention is \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), with \(z\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\exists(x,y,z):Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\ z\ge0\iff\exists d:Qd=0,\ Ad=0,\ Gd\le0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d=-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Stationarity Alternative for a Convex QP

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Qd=0\), \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), and \(c^Td<0\) certify infeasibility of the dual KKT system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession-direction certificate excluding dual feasibility for a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex QP with constraints \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), a nonzero vector \(d\) satisfying \(Qd=0\), \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), and \(c^Td<0\) is a certificate of dual infeasibility. If dual KKT multipliers \((y,z)\) with \(z\ge0\) existed, stationarity paired with \(d\) would give \(c^Td=-z^TGd\ge0\), contradicting \(c^Td<0\). The certificate also identifies a decreasing feasible recession direction whenever the primal feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-curvature feasible recession direction with strictly negative linear cost contradicts dual stationarity and therefore certifies dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direction conditions do contradict dual stationarity under the stated sign convention, and certificate is an appropriate kind. A source is required to establish the precise QP status terminology and hypotheses.

children.title: Unboundedness Rays
children.top_down_role: Recession evidence supporting an unbounded primal objective status.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and interval-validated sufficient conditions for a convex-QP unboundedness ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\hat x\) be a verified feasible point and \(\hat d\ne0\). Verify \(A\hat d=0\), \(G\hat d\le0\), \(\hat d^{\mathsf T}Q\hat d=0\), and \((Q\hat x+c)^{\mathsf T}\hat d<0\). Then \(\hat x+t\hat d\) is feasible for every \(t\ge0\) and its objective tends to \(-\infty\). With inexact data or arithmetic, interval or backward-error bounds must establish the recession relations, zero curvature, and a strictly negative entire slope enclosure; residual magnitudes without verified signs are insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible base point and a rigorously validated zero-curvature improving recession direction certify primal unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: Any inexact coefficient enclosures account for data and arithmetic errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \hat x+t\hat d\text{ is feasible for all }t\ge0\text{ and }f(\hat x+t\hat d)\to-\infty.

notation.meaning: Validated feasible base point and recession direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Aware Ray Validation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limits of candidate recession-direction evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direction satisfying homogeneous recession and descent conditions does not certify primal unboundedness unless a primal feasible base point is also verified. Conversely, rejection of one candidate direction, or failure of a numerical search to find one, does not certify boundedness below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unboundedness needs both a feasible base point and a valid improving ray; failure to find a ray is not a boundedness certificate.
assumptions_latex: QP status is determined by finite certificate validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\text{ alone}\not\Rightarrow\inf f=-\infty,\qquad \text{rejected or missing }d\not\Rightarrow\inf f> -\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Ray Evidence Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive unboundedness certificate for a feasible convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0\) satisfy \(Ax_0=b\) and \(Gx_0\le h\). If a nonzero \(d\) satisfies \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^Td<0\), then \(x(t)=x_0+td\) is feasible for every \(t\ge0\). Because \(Q\succeq0\) and \(Qd=0\), also \(x_0^TQd=0\), and therefore \(f(x(t))=f(x_0)+t c^Td\to-\infty\). Thus \((x_0,d)\) is a directly verifiable unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point plus a zero-curvature feasible recession direction of negative linear cost certifies that the convex QP objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Rays

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-ray calculation and unboundedness conclusion are mathematically coherent, but the record has no supporting source or standard-field rationale. A specific authoritative locator is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract status split for a normalized homogeneous self-dual QP embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a normalized homogeneous self-dual embedding, let \(\tau,\kappa\ge0\) be the solution and certificate scalars. If \(\tau>0\) and \(\kappa=0\), division of the embedded primal-dual variables by \(\tau\) yields a primal-dual KKT solution. children.title: Newton-Solve Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Residual and error regimes for approximate primal-dual Newton directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning-dependent conversion of a Newton linear-system residual into step error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\Delta=-F\), let \(K\) be nonsingular, and define \(e=K\widehat\Delta+F\). Then \(\widehat\Delta-\Delta=K^{-1}e\) and, for any subordinate norm, \[\|\widehat\Delta-\Delta\|\leq\|K^{-1}\|\,\|e\|.\] If \(F\neq0\), then \[\frac{\|\widehat\Delta-\Delta\|}{\|\Delta\|}\leq\kappa(K)\frac{\|e\|}{\|F\|},\qquad \kappa(K)=\|K\|\,\|K^{-1}\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small Newton-equation residual controls step error only after amplification by the inverse or condition number of the Newton matrix.
assumptions_latex: The matrix norm is subordinate to the selected vector norm

notation.meaning: Condition number in the selected subordinate norm

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Step Error Bound

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|K_k\widehat\Delta_k+F_k\|\le\eta_k\|F_k\|\) certifies the requested relative Newton-solve accuracy.

notation.meaning: KKT or Newton matrix at outer iteration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative residual condition for an inexact primal-dual Newton solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), let the exact Newton equation be \(K_k\Delta_k=-F_k\). A computed step \(\widehat\Delta_k\) has relative residual accuracy \(\eta_k\) when its linear residual \(e_k=K_k\widehat\Delta_k+F_k\) satisfies \(\|e_k\|\le\eta_k\|F_k\|\), where \(0\le\eta_k<1\). For a preconditioned iterative solve, the same condition must be evaluated in the explicitly chosen preconditioned norm. This condition is checkable without knowing the exact Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact Newton step meets its requested accuracy when the residual of the linearized KKT equation is at most a prescribed fraction of the outer residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Solve Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative linear-residual condition is standard and the condition kind fits the leaf, but no evidence record or authoritative locator supports it. The norm and preconditioning convention must also be tied to the cited formulation.

children.title: Outer Stopping Reliability
children.top_down_role: Trustworthiness of QP termination decisions under inexact linear solves.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Three-Way Stopping Decision Under Additive Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe acceptance, safe rejection, and the indeterminate band under a certified additive residual-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\widehat F=F+e\), \(\|e\|\leq\delta\), and \(\varepsilon>\delta\). Then \(\|\widehat F\|\leq\varepsilon-\delta\) guarantees \(\|F\|\leq\varepsilon\), while \(\|\widehat F\|>\varepsilon+\delta\) guarantees \(\|F\|>\varepsilon\). If \(\varepsilon-\delta<\|\widehat F\|\leq\varepsilon+\delta\), the additive bound alone permits exact residuals on both sides of the stopping threshold and therefore supports neither a guaranteed acceptance nor a guaranteed rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified error radius creates safe acceptance and rejection regions separated by an indeterminate stopping band.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is safe below \(\varepsilon-\delta\), rejection is safe above \(\varepsilon+\delta\), and the intervening band is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.title: Three-Way Stopping Decision Under Additive Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Margin rule preventing inner or evaluation error from causing premature outer termination.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced matrix-free Newton operator is symmetric positive semidefinite and is positive definite precisely when the Hessian and constraint term have no common null direction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adjoint-Consistency Boundary for Symmetric Matrix-Free Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry requirement for reduced Newton operators implemented with separately coded forward and transpose products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an implemented reduced action be \(\widetilde H v=Qv+\widetilde G^{\mathsf T}(D(Gv))\). If the routine denoted \(\widetilde G^{\mathsf T}\) is not the Euclidean adjoint of the implemented forward routine \(G\), then \(\widetilde H\) need not be symmetric even when \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\) and \(D\succ0\). Consequently, symmetry-dependent Krylov guarantees cannot be invoked without adjoint consistency or an explicitly nonsymmetric solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separately implemented transpose product must be the actual adjoint of the forward product; otherwise the nominally symmetric Newton operator may be nonsymmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde G^{\mathsf T}\ne G^*\ \Longrightarrow\ \widetilde H\text{ need not be symmetric}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact substitution condensing requires the retained variables and fixed data to determine every eliminated variable uniquely. If the defining affine equations leave free eliminated directions, no single affine map parameterizes all feasible points and direct substitution can discard feasible solutions. The free directions must instead be retained, parameterized, or removed only after an explicitly equivalent reduction.

Even when the uncondensed stagewise KKT matrix is block banded, propagation through \(\Gamma\) can make the condensed Hessian and constraints dense. Full condensing therefore reduces dimension while potentially increasing storage, fill, and conditioning difficulty; partial condensing interpolates between the sparse and fully condensed regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) stages have state dimension \(n_x\) and control dimension \(n_u\), with fixed \(x_0\) excluded and \(L\mid T\). If states strictly inside each group of \(L\) stages are eliminated while every control and each group-end state are retained, then \[N_{\mathrm{pc}}=Tn_u+\frac{T}{L}n_x.\] Thus \(L=1\) gives \(T(n_u+n_x)\), while \(L=T\) retains \(Tn_u+n_x\); additionally eliminating the terminal state gives the fully control-condensed count \(Tn_u\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual correspondence for block-elimination condensing and reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition a Newton system as \[\begin{bmatrix}K_{ee}&K_{er}\\K_{re}&K_{rr}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}d_e\\d_r\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}b_e\\b_r\end{bmatrix},\qquad K_{ee}\text{ nonsingular}.\] Set \(S=K_{rr}-K_{re}K_{ee}^{-1}K_{er}\), \(\widehat b=b_r-K_{re}K_{ee}^{-1}b_e\), and reconstruct \(d_e=K_{ee}^{-1}(b_e-K_{er}d_r)\). Then \[b-Kd=\begin{bmatrix}0\\\widehat b-Sd_r\end{bmatrix}.\] Thus a condensed residual is an original-system residual only under exact eliminated-variable reconstruction; otherwise both original residual blocks must be tested.

Successive exact substitution into every objective and constraint produces the same reduced QP in \(r\) as first composing the affine maps and then substituting once. Thus exact partial-condensing groups may be merged or subdivided without changing the reduced feasible set, objective values, or reconstructed original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive exact affine eliminations and their one-shot composition produce the same reduced QP.
assumptions_latex: Every elimination map is single-valued and affine.
All substitutions use exact arithmetic and consistent variable ordering.

The full matrix \(K\) may nevertheless be nonsingular when a proposed \(B_i\) is singular; independent elimination is then invalid and requires a different partition, null-space treatment, cross-boundary pivoting, or declared regularization.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular two-by-two bordered matrix can have a singular proposed local block, invalidating independent local elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsingular Full System with a Singular Local Pivot
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingular Full System with a Singular Local Pivot

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact determinant, inertia, and nonsingularity identities for an independently eliminable symmetric bordered system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}B&E\\E^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\) with symmetric nonsingular \(B\), define \(S=C-E^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}E\). Then \[\det K=\det B\,\det S,\qquad \operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(B)+\operatorname{inertia}(S).\] In particular, \(K\) is nonsingular if and only if \(S\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating nonsingular local blocks transfers determinant, inertia, and nonsingularity information exactly to the coupling Schur complement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative bordered-block reduction obtained by eliminating the coupling block first.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}B&E\\E^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\) with nonsingular \(C\), define \(T=B-EC^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[Tp=f-EC^{-1}g,\qquad q=C^{-1}(g-E^{\mathsf T}p).\] Moreover, \(\det K=\det C\det T\), and, for symmetric \(K\), \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(C)+\operatorname{inertia}(T)\). This reduction is exact but generally couples the formerly independent blocks of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible coupling block may be eliminated first, although this generally destroys local block independence.
assumptions_latex: Permutations and regularization are applied consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ is nonsingular}\iff T=B-EC^{-1}E^{\mathsf T}\text{ is nonsingular}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori accuracy test for local elimination, coupling solution, and block recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[K=\begin{bmatrix}B&E\\E^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix},\qquad K\binom{p}{q}=\binom{f}{g},\] define \[r_p=f-Bp-Eq,\qquad r_q=g-E^{\mathsf T}p-Cq.\] Then \(r=(r_p,r_q)\) is exactly the residual of the original bordered system, independently of how the local and coupling solves were performed. Thus \(r_p=r_q=0\) if and only if \((p,q)\) solves that system. When the denominator is positive, a normwise acceptance test is \[\frac{\|r\|}{\|K\|\,\|(p,q)\|+\|(f,g)\|}\le\tau.\] Residual assembly must use the same permutation and regularization as the system whose solution is claimed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reassemble the local and coupling residuals in the intended bordered equations; their combined normalized norm certifies the computed block-decomposition solution.
assumptions_latex: The tested matrix, permutation, right-hand side, and regularization are those intended by the Newton step.
All local and coupling products required for residual assembly are available.
\(\|K\|\|(p,q)\|+\|(f,g)\|>0\) when the normalized test is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_p=r_q=0\iff K(p,q)^{\mathsf T}=(f,g)^{\mathsf T},\quad\text{and the displayed ratio certifies the declared normalized residual tolerance}.
knowledge_statements.title: Original-Equation Residual Certificate for Block Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign and rank structure of coupling updates generated by positive-definite local blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\operatorname{diag}(B_1,\ldots,B_N)\) with \(B_i\succ0\), and partition \(E=(E_1^{\mathsf T},\ldots,E_N^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\). Then every local coupling update \(U_i=E_i^{\mathsf T}B_i^{-1}E_i\) is positive semidefinite and \[\operatorname{rank}(U_i)\le\operatorname{rank}(E_i).\] Consequently, \(C-S=\sum_iU_i\succeq0\) for \(S=C-E^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating positive-definite local blocks subtracts a sum of positive-semidefinite, rank-limited updates from the coupling block.

notation.meaning: Schur update contributed by local block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Local Schur Updates

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\begin{bmatrix}B&E\\E^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\binom{p}{q}=\binom{f}{g},\qquad B=\operatorname{diag}(B_1,\ldots,B_N),\] with every \(B_i\) nonsingular, independently compute \(u_i=B_i^{-1}f_i\) and the actions needed for \(E_i^{\mathsf T}B_i^{-1}E_i\). Assemble \[S=C-\sum_iE_i^{\mathsf T}B_i^{-1}E_i,\qquad h=g-\sum_iE_i^{\mathsf T}u_i,\] solve \(Sq=h\), and recover \(p_i=B_i^{-1}(f_i-E_iq)\) independently. Required pivots are nonsingular and do not force fill outside the stated band.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a symmetric block-banded Newton matrix with \(T\) temporal block rows, uniform block size \(p\), and block half-bandwidth \(w\). If elimination proceeds without pivots or regularization that create fill outside this band, dense-block \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization requires \(O(Tw^2p^3)\) arithmetic and stores \(O(Twp^2)\) factor entries; forward and backward substitutions require \(O(Twp^2)\) arithmetic. Thus the cost is linear in \(T\) for fixed \(p\) and \(w\).

With uniform block size \(p\) and dense block arithmetic, the ideal bounds are \(O(Tp^3)\) work and \(O(p^3\log T)\) arithmetic span.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel cyclic reduction recursively eliminates alternating stages while preserving block-tridiagonal structure.
assumptions_latex: The temporal Newton matrix is block tridiagonal.
Every eliminated pivot at every level is nonsingular.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riccati–Temporal Elimination Equivalence for Linear-Quadratic Stages
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Riccati representation of block elimination for an unconstrained finite-horizon linear-quadratic subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the QP \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), suppose a solver returns \((x,y,z)\) with \(z\ge0\) and scaled residual \(r_{\mathrm{KKT}}\le\varepsilon\). This inequality is only a backward-error test. If \(\kappa_D\varepsilon\) is not small, it need not imply a small forward error or objective error. Moreover, neither primal infeasibility nor dual infeasibility is established without a separately normalized alternative-system certificate, and unboundedness is not established without a feasible recession direction \(d\) satisfying \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^\top d<0\). Thus the status must remain numerically ambiguous when these discriminating tests fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small scaled KKT residuals can coexist with large solution error. Without separate infeasibility or recession certificates and acceptable conditioning, the solver must report an ambiguous status.
knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Numerical Status
